battle.name: 邵興抗金起義
battle.theater: 解州神稷山寨與陝州前線
battle.brief: 靖康二年（1127）汴京陷落，北宋覆亡，北方郡縣淪入金人之手。解州安邑人邵興聚眾於神稷山築寨自保，屢挫金軍追剿；金人擒其弟邵翼相脅，他不屈服，照常出戰。紹興元年陝州失守後，他突圍南下，改名邵隆，退守商州十年。卡面的希臘火不在河東戰場上，當年燒過的是火矢與火箭。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 這場起義發生在南宋初年北方淪陷區，交戰的兩端是金朝控制下的河東官軍與民間抗金義軍。金一方是完顏女真建立的金朝：靖康二年（1127）金軍第二次南征，粘罕與完顏宗望分道南下，汴京陷落之後，金廷扶植漢人官員治理新占之地，設河東、西京等路，地方以女真猛安、謀克為骨幹，配以編戶的漢軍與降附將士，解州一線由河東各處屯軍分守，鎮守任務多派給降軍與地方鎮兵。金方在起義初期以招撫與進剿並行：能招則招，拒撫則遣騎兵搜討山寨、斷其糧道。南宋一方此刻在北方幾乎沒有地面軍隊，高宗於建炎元年五月在南京應天府即位，中樞的實際控制力止於淮南，北方僅存零星官軍與大批自發的義軍。邵興的隊伍便屬於這一類：自解州鄉里聚合、以寨自守的民兵性質隊伍，無正式番號，糧餉多靠自備與就食河東農村，後期受趙鼎、張浚主持的荊陝宣撫司招撫，授招討、統制一類名銜，取得部分官給與名義上的旗號，另與楚州張榮、睦州曹勛等同輩義師互為聲援，但彼此之間從無統一指揮。
countriesEn: This uprising took place in the northern districts that had just passed to the Jin, with the Jin-controlled military administration of Hedong on one side and the anti-Jin volunteers of the Chinese countryside on the other. The Jin side was the state founded by the Jurchen Wanyan clan: in the second Jin invasion of 1127, Nianhan and Wanyan Zongwang marched south by two separate routes, and after Bianjing fell the Jin court installed Han Chinese officials to govern the new territory, creating circuits such as Hedong and Xijing. At the local level the Jurchen meng'an and mouke units formed the backbone, supplemented by registered Han troops and surrendered former Song soldiers; the garrison line around Jiezhou was divided between detachments drawn from the surrendered army and the local regional troops, and most of the holding duties fell to them. In the opening phase the Jin combined amnesty with pursuit: those who came in were enrolled, those who refused were hunted by cavalry raiding the mountain stockades and cutting their supply lines. The Southern Song side, in practice, had no field army left in the north. Gaozong took the throne at Nanjing Yingtian fu in the fifth month of Jianyan (1127), and the effective reach of the central government stopped at the Huai river; only scattered regular units and a great many self-raised bands remained in the north. Shao Xing's command belonged to the latter category: a militia kind of force assembled from the villages of Jiezhou, holding a stockade on its own, without an official designation, living off its own resources and off the Hedong countryside, and only later taken into the Song military order by the Jing and Shaan pacification commission under Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun, which granted titles such as zhaotai and tongzhi together with a little official pay and a nominal banner. Shao Xing's band thus echoed contemporaries such as Zhang Rong at Chuzhou and Cao Xun at Muzhou, but no central command ever tied them together.
people: 邵興（一〇九五至一一四五），字晉卿，解州安邑（今山西運城）人，鄉人稱他邵大伯，是這場起義的旗幟人物。靖康之變後他在解州神稷山築寨自保，屢次擊退金軍追剿；金人一度擒獲他的弟弟邵翼，用來相脅他投降，他不從，照常出戰，義軍因此沒有散。金廷扶植劉豫建偽齊後，他率部南下轉入陝州前線，隸屬守將李彥仙，紹興元年（一一三〇）末陝州失守，李彥仙殉國，他突圍南奔，改名邵隆，退守商州，在那裡又堅守十年。和議成後他仍常化裝遣人出擊金兵，招致主和派猜忌，最終被秦檜以毒藥殺害，終年五十。楚州義軍首領張榮是他的同期同道：張榮於罷馬山起兵，眾至數萬，一一二八年金軍圍楚州，張榮登城拒守數月，迫金兵退走；兩人同在南宋朝廷的招撫名錄上，卻各守一方、互不相屬。南宋丞相趙鼎是招撫二人並重建荊襄秩序的關鍵人物，張浚以經略使出師川陝，是把邵興部收進南宋軍事序列的人。金人一側，粘罕（完顏宗翰）與完顏宗望是靖康二年南征的主帥，河東方面的進剿則由各路留守將領分段執行。此外還有大批由北方逃難而來、被金軍打散而重新聚合的將校與鄉勇頭目，被趙鼎與地方宣撫司收編後成為義軍的骨幹；邵興能在陝州站住腳，靠的正是這批人。
peopleEn: Shao Xing (1095-1145), courtesy name Jinqing, was a native of Anyi in Jiezhou, in present-day Yuncheng, Shanxi, and the villagers called him Elder Shao. He became the banner figure of this uprising. After the Jingkang disaster he built a stockade on Mount Shenji near Jiezhou and held it against the Jin, beating back repeated punitive expeditions; the Jin at one point seized his younger brother Shao Yi and used the man to force his surrender, and Shao Xing refused, kept his men in the field and did not disband, so that the band held together. After the Jin court set up Liu Yu's puppet state of Qi, he led his force south and moved into the Shaan front, where he served under the garrison commander Li Yanxian. When Shaan prefecture fell in the last months of Shaoxing (1130) and Li Yanxian died defending it, Shao Xing broke out to the south, changed his name to Shao Long and withdrew to Shang prefecture, where he held out for another ten years. After the peace settlement he still habitually sent men out disguised to raid Jin troops, which alarmed the peace party, and he was finally killed by poison administered by Qin Hui, dying at the age of fifty. Zhang Rong, leader of the Chuzhou volunteers, was his contemporary and fellow traveller: Zhang Rong raised men at Baima mountain with a following said to number in the tens of thousands, and when the Jin besieged Chuzhou in 1128 he took the city walls and held them for several months until the besiegers withdrew. Both men stood on the Song court's list of pacified insurgents, yet each held his own ground and neither answered to the other. Zhao Ding, chancellor of the Southern Song, was the key figure in bringing the two of them in and rebuilding the Jingxiang order, while Zhang Jun, as pacification commissioner, was the man who pulled Shao Xing's command into the Southern Song military order. On the Jin side, Nianhan, that is Wanyan Zonghan, and Wanyan Zongwang were the commanders of the invasion of 1127, while in Hedong the pursuit was carried out in sections by the regional garrison commanders. Alongside them were many officers and village militia leaders who had fled north, been scattered by the Jin, and gathered again; pacified by Zhao Ding and the local commissions, they formed the backbone of the insurgents, and it was on them that Shao Xing's stand at Shaan depended.
kits: 卡面這件希臘火是拜占庭帝國的國策級裝備：相傳七世紀末君士坦丁堡的工匠試成了灌在銅管、以虹吸管推出的燃燒劑，第一次成規模使用見於六七八年前後的敘利亞沿海戰役，此後數百年是帝國對付阿拉伯與突厥系海陸手的招牌，配方屬帝國最高機密，工藝隨戰船一起沉進海底，到十二世紀已不再有可靠的使用紀錄。它並不在河東戰場上，這一點必須講清楚：一二二七年的解州、陝州一線，沒有任何一方使用過這類噴射式縱火器材。當年真正在場的是兩套完全不同的縱火技術。中國這邊，宋代兵書已載有火藥箭與毒煙、火炮之屬，義軍與官軍夜襲、焚糧、燒攻城具，用的是火矢、火箭、火炬與營火；西方這邊，希臘火走的是石油瀝青一系的噴射路子，靠銅管與壓力把火送出去。兩條技術路徑彼此無涉，火藥是隨蒙古軍西征才在十三世紀進入歐洲，希臘火則在拜占庭衰亡時失傳。除了火，金屬裝備同樣有限：雙方主力是冷兵器，長槊、大刀、狼牙棒配小圜盾與長牌，射手用角弓與踏張弩，披札甲、皮甲，河東義軍的馬匹少，靠步行作戰、靠驢騾馱糧。金軍備有石砲一類的拋射機具攻寨，攻城則用撞車、雲梯與排梯，義軍以木石拒馬、柴草塞隘、火箭焚攻具應對；糧秣方面，義軍多靠就食、掠敵糧與屯墾，官軍接應後才有宣撫款項接濟。
kitsEn: The Greek fire on this card was a state-level weapon of the Byzantine Empire: according to tradition a craftsman in Constantinople at the end of the seventh century produced a burning mixture that was poured into copper tubes and pushed out through a siphon, its first large-scale use being recorded around 678 in the fighting along the Syrian coast. For several centuries it was the empire's signature weapon against Arab and Turkic opponents at sea and on land. The formula was the empire's highest secret, the craft went down with the warships that carried it, and by the twelfth century there is no reliable record of it being used. It was not present on the Hedong battlefield, and that has to be stated plainly: on the Jiezhou and Shaan lines in 1127 no side whatsoever employed a projection incendiary of that kind. What was actually present were two entirely different technologies of setting fire. On the Chinese side, Song military manuals already carried entries for gunpowder arrows, smoke shells and small bombs, and the insurgents and regulars who raided by night, fired granaries and burned siege gear used fire arrows, gunpowder arrows, torches and campfires. In the West, Greek fire followed the petroleum-and-bitumen line, delivering the fire through copper tubing and pressure. The two technical lines had no contact with one another: gunpowder only reached Europe in the thirteenth century riding with the armies of the Mongols, while Greek fire was lost as the Byzantine state declined. Metal equipment was equally scarce on both sides. Cold weapons formed the core of every formation: long spears, glaives, wolf-toothed clubs, small round shields and long shields, with composite bows and strong crossbows for the archers, and lamellar and leather armour. The Hedong insurgents had few horses, fought on foot and moved their supplies on donkeys and mules. The Jin had stone-throwing engines for hammering at stockades and used battering rams, scaling ladders and assault towers against walls; the insurgents answered with felled timber and stones to stop horses, brushwood and straw wedged into the passes, and fire arrows to burn the siege gear. For grain they largely relied on foraging, seizing enemy stores and cultivation, and only after the regular army took them over did the pacification commission actually pay them in supplies.
tactics: 邵興這一套是典型的山寨守禦加游擊破襲。寨子築在神稷山的脊背上，依山就勢，前後只留一條能上下的通道，寨牆以木柵、夯土夾雜石塊砌成，隘口用橫木與鹿角阻擋，坡面削成陡坎以絕騎兵。起義之初眾寡懸殊，義軍不與金軍在平地決鬥，只在山道、峽口與關隘設伏：待金騎進入狹窄地帶再以矢石、落木擾亂其陣，隨即由兩側高處以長槊、弓弩壓下來，追擊只在敵隊形散亂時進行，奪獲馬匹、鎧甲與糧秣即退回山寨。金軍對付山寨的辦法是先以石砲遠射、再以步卒列陣仰攻，義軍則以柴薪塞住隘口、以火箭與火矢焚燒貼近的雲梯與撞車，趁夜由缺口出擊焚燒金軍的營帳與糧車。轉戰陝州之後，義軍被編入守城序列，戰法轉為依托城池的守禦與巷戰：守軍分段節制，牆頭列弓弩，火力交叉覆蓋城下通道，攻城金軍一旦逼近就以火箭灼其攻具，被壓制時退入街巷逐段抵抗。退守商州之後，邵興的隊伍又回到他最熟悉的路子：守山城、避主力、專挑落單的騎隊與糧隊下手，斷金軍在關中的補給線。
tacticsEn: Shao Xing's method was classic stockade defence combined with raiding and harassment. The camp was built along the spine of Mount Shenji, shaped to the terrain, with only one route up and down; the wall was made of timber palisades, rammed earth and rough stone, the passes blocked with transverse timbers and antler obstacles, and the slopes cut into steep scarps to turn cavalry. In the opening phase the insurgents were badly outnumbered and never met the Jin in the open. They ambushed in the mountain tracks, the gullies and the passes: letting the Jin horse enter the narrow ground, then disordering the column with arrows, stones and felled timber before pressing down from the heights on both sides with long spears and crossbows. Pursuit was carried out only while the enemy formation was broken, and as soon as horses, armour and provisions were taken, the band fell back into the stockade. The Jin method against such a position was to open with stone-throwing engines at long range and then send foot soldiers up in formation; the insurgents answered by wedging firewood into the passes, burning scaling ladders and battering rams that came close with fire arrows and fire lances, and by sallying from a breach at night to burn the Jin camp tents and grain carts. After the move into Shaan the band was folded into the garrison order and the style of war changed to defence of a walled city and street fighting: the garrison was organised in sections, archers were posted along the walls with overlapping fields of fire covering the approaches below, the assaulting troops of the Jin were met with fire arrows against their siege gear whenever they got close, and when overborne the defenders withdrew into the streets and resisted house by house. After the retreat to Shang prefecture the command went back to what Shao Xing knew best: hold the hill town, avoid pitched battle, pick off isolated cavalry columns and supply trains, and cut the Jin supply line through the Guanzhong region.
data: 關於人數，史料留下的數字本身互相矛盾，需要照單全收的警告。金人南征的兵力，漢文記載從八十萬到數十萬乃至數萬都有，比較可靠的做法是把它理解為兩路大軍各率數萬精騎作骨幹，輔以十萬量級的步卒、降軍與運糧人夫，真正投入攻城與追剿的戰鬥兵員當然遠小於戰報上的數字。義軍方面，邵興聚眾的說法多在數千至數萬之間，地方記載稱眾至數萬，但義軍的編制以寨為單位、每寨數百至數千人，且大量成員是農民與被金軍打散的散兵，戰鬥力與裝備參差極大；同期的楚州張榮部眾亦被記為數萬，兩支部伍加總佔據了淮南與河東的鄉村。距離與時間可以算得比較清楚：解州距汴京約五百餘公里，距陝州約二百公里，陝州至商州再往西南約三百公里；邵興自一一二七年起事，到一一三〇年末陝州失守南撤，再守商州十年，最終在一一四五年被毒殺，從起義到結束橫跨十八年。關鍵節點也有紀年：一一二七年一月汴京陷落，同年五月高宗在南京應天府即位，一一三〇年末陝州淪陷、李彥仙殉國，一一四一年宋金和議，一一四五年邵興被秦檜毒殺。官軍與義軍的具體損耗沒有可核的數字，只留下屢挫金軍、追剿不止這類概括的記載。
dataEn: On numbers, the sources contradict one another and the tally has to be taken with care. Chinese accounts of the strength of the Jin armies of 1127 range from eight hundred thousand down to a few tens of thousands and even to mere thousands; the more defensible reading is that each of the two columns led by several tens of thousands of cavalry, backed by foot soldiers, surrendered troops and baggage trains on a scale of hundreds of thousands, while the actual combat manpower committed to sieges and pursuit was far below the figures in the reports. On the insurgent side, estimates of Shao Xing's following run from a few thousand to tens of thousands, and local accounts speak of tens of thousands; the organisation, however, was by stockade, each holding from several hundred to a few thousand men, and a large part of the rank and file were peasants and soldiers scattered by the Jin, so that fighting quality and equipment varied enormously. The Chuzhou band of Zhang Rong is likewise recorded with tens of thousands; together these two commands covered the villages of the Huai and Hedong regions. Distances and duration can be set down more firmly: from Jiezhou to Bianjing is a little over five hundred kilometres, from Jiezhou to Shaan prefecture about two hundred, and from Shaan to Shang prefecture another three hundred to the south-west. Shao Xing raised his band in 1127, was driven south when Shaan fell in the last months of 1130, held Shang prefecture for ten years more, and was poisoned in 1145, so the whole business spans eighteen years. The key nodes are dated as well: Bianjing fell in January 1127; Gaozong took the throne at Nanjing Yingtian fu in May of the same year; Shaan prefecture fell at the end of 1130 and Li Yanxian died with it; the Song-Jin peace was concluded in 1141; and Qin Hui poisoned Shao Xing in 1145. There are no verifiable figures for the losses on either side, only such general statements as that the Jin were repeatedly checked and that the pursuit never stopped.
cause: 起義的直接背景是靖康之變。靖康元年冬到靖康二年（一一二六至一一二七）金軍第二次南征，連下衛州、拱辰門、汴京，徽、欽二帝被俘，北宋在名義上覆亡，河東、河北、山東大片郡縣在數月之內淪陷，地方秩序、糧餉與軍制同時崩解。對淪陷區的鄉民與散兵而言，留在原地意味著被編入金人的漢軍、輸送糧草或者淪為驅役；聚眾自保、據山寨以抗金，於是最先出現在河東的解州與淮南北部的楚州一帶，與嶺南、浙東的曹勛、楊幺起義合流成一片。深一層的原因是金廷無法真正消化新占之地：它倚賴漢人官員治理，靠降軍維持地方，卻要面對一支在山中自組織起來的武裝，這支部隊切斷驛道、掠走糧車、隨時可能襲擊屯軍，任何一次進剿都可能把新得的河東再弄亂，於是金人一面招撫、一面進剿，條件是解散山寨、歸編為軍。南宋朝廷這邊鞭長莫及，北方地面沒有一支能調動的官軍，唯一的辦法是把這些義軍收編：授以招討、統制等名銜，給少量旗號與糧餉，讓他們替朝廷守住淮南與關中的缺口。這一來雙方都想利用對方，一來雙方也都防著對方，衝突從此長期化。
causeEn: The immediate background was the Jingkang disaster. Between the winter of 1126 and 1127 the Jin invaded for a second time, took Weizhou, broke through the Gongchen gate and entered Bianjing; the emperors Hui and Qin were taken prisoner, the Northern Song ceased to exist in name, and large stretches of Hedong, Hebei and Shandong passed out of Song control within a few months, destroying the local order, its supply system and its military administration at the same time. For the villagers and scattered soldiers of the occupied districts, staying put meant being enrolled in the Jin Chinese army, hauling grain for the enemy, or being driven into servitude. The answer that spread first in Hedong around Jiezhou and along the northern Huai at Chuzhou was to gather men, hold a mountain stockade and fight the Jin, joining up with the risings of Cao Xun and Yang Yao in Lingnan and eastern Zhejiang. At a deeper level the Jin court could not digest what it had taken: it governed through Han Chinese officials and maintained order with surrendered troops, while facing an armed force that organised itself in the hills, cut the postal roads, seized grain carts and could strike garrisons at any moment. Any punitive expedition risked undoing the recent conquest of Hedong, so the Jin offered amnesty and sent in the army at the same time, on condition that the stockades be dissolved and the bands enrolled. The Southern Song, for its part, could not reach that far: there was no regular army on the northern ground it could move, and the only available method was to absorb the insurgents, granting titles such as zhaotai and tongzhi, a token of banners and some pay, and setting them to hold the gaps in the Huai defences and in Guanzhong. Each side meant to use the other, and each side also feared the other, which is why the conflict ran on for so long.
impact: 起義的直接效果，是在金軍最需要穩定後方的年份裡，讓河東與淮南的鄉村沒有全部落入金人之手。解州山寨把金軍的追剿一次次拖成持久戰，迫使金廷把本可用於南線的騎兵一部份釘在河東；楚州方面張榮守城逼退金兵，淮南門戶也因之未失。義軍的存在同時推動了金朝以漢人傀儡治漢地的政策，一一三〇年劉豫偽齊成立，正是金廷在無法直接治理的情況下推出的替代辦法，義軍的騷擾是這項政策背後的重要壓力。放到更長的時間裡，這批起義塑造了南宋開國頭二十年的邊區格局：北方流民自建武力、地方豪族趁勢而起，南宋政府不得不放下正統的架子去與他們打交道，招撫、編軍、給銜、供糧這套做法此後成為南朝處理北方義軍的固定套路。另一面的代價在政治上：紹興和議一成，秦檧一派開始清算義軍出身的將領，邵興被毒殺即是一例，義軍在官方敘事裡被定性為群盜而非義士，北宋末南渡初累積起來的民間抗金記憶因此被系統性抹去，這種對北方民心的疏離一直影響到隆興、開禧兩次北伐的士氣。技術史上，這場起義也留下了一個對照：同一個年代，希臘火在拜占庭走到盡頭、配方隨帝國沉沒，而中國的火箭與火藥武器正在民間手裡散開並越來越常見，兩種縱火技術在十三世紀分別走向了不同的結局。
impactEn: The direct effect of the uprising was that, in the very years when the Jin most needed a quiet rear, the villages of Hedong and the Huai did not all pass into Jin hands. The stockades of Jiezhou turned every punitive expedition into a long war of attrition and forced the Jin court to pin down a share of the cavalry that could have been used on the southern front; on the Chuzhou side, Zhang Rong's defence of the city drove the besiegers off, and the Huai gateway was saved. At the same time the insurgents pressed the Jin towards ruling the Chinese through a Chinese puppet: the establishment of Liu Yu's state of Qi in 1130 was the alternative the Jin court resorted to when it could not govern directly, and the harassment of the volunteers was a large part of the pressure behind that policy. Over a longer span these risings shaped the borderlands of the first two decades of the Southern Song: refugees in the north raised their own armed bands, local strongmen took advantage of the confusion, and the Song government had to set aside its claims to legitimacy in order to deal with them. Pacifying, numbering, paying and feeding them became the fixed routine by which the southern court handled northern insurgents from then on. The cost lay on the political side. Once the Shaoxing peace was made, Qin Hui's faction began to liquidate officers who had come out of the volunteer bands, and the poisoning of Shao Xing is a case in point; in official narrative the insurgents were recast as bandits rather than patriots, and the anti-Jin memory accumulated in the last years of the Northern Song and the first years of the south was systematically erased. That alienation of the northern populace weighed on the morale of the later Longxing and Kaixi northern expeditions. In the history of technology the uprising leaves a contrast as well: in the same decades Greek fire reached the end of its road in Byzantium, its formula sinking with the empire, while in China the fire arrow and gunpowder weapons were spreading through civilian hands and growing common; by the thirteenth century the two technologies of incendiary warfare had headed toward very different ends.
result: 結果沒有漂亮的勝負可以寫下：一一二七到一一三〇年間，邵興的義軍在解州神稷山站穩了寨，屢次挫敗金軍追剿，卻始終沒有能力收復河東，也沒有被金人消滅；金廷在河東的實際控制長期停留在州縣與驛道一線，山寨之間的鄉村由義軍維持著一種脆弱的自治。紹興元年（一一三〇）末陝州失守、李彥仙殉國，邵興率殘部突圍南下，改名邵隆退守商州，又在那座秦嶺山中的州城裡堅守近十年，間或出擊金軍的糧道與巡隊。宋金和議於一一四一年成立後，和平局面下他仍不斷化裝遣人襲擾金兵，義軍的戰法與存在本身成了主和派最不放心的東西，一一四五年秦檜用毒藥結果了邵興，這支部隊隨之解體，殘部或散歸鄉里，或被收編入南宋的地方屯軍。以單場起義論，它既沒有改變宋金對峙的大局，也沒有被寫進任何一場決定性的會戰，但它守住的那幾座山寨、拖住的那幾年時間，在南宋開國最虛弱的二十年裡，是北方唯一還在運作的抵抗力量，也讓後來的讀者記得：在正式的官軍之外，抗金從來沒有真正停止過。
resultEn: There is no neat result to set down. Between 1127 and 1130 Shao Xing's band held its stockade on Mount Shenji near Jiezhou and repeatedly checked Jin punitive expeditions, yet it never had the strength to recover Hedong and was never destroyed by the Jin either; the Jin court's real control in Hedong stayed for years on the level of the prefectures and the postal roads, while the villages between the stockades were kept in a fragile state of self-government by the insurgents themselves. When Shaan prefecture fell at the end of Shaoxing (1130) and Li Yanxian died in its defence, Shao Xing led the remnants out to the south, changed his name to Shao Long and withdrew to Shang prefecture, where he held out for close to another ten years in that walled seat among the Qinling mountains, striking now and then at the Jin supply lines and patrols. The Song-Jin peace was concluded in 1141, and even in peacetime he kept sending men out disguised to harass Jin troops; the very method of the insurgents and the fact of their existence were what the peace party feared most, and in 1145 Qin Hui ended Shao Xing with poison. The band then dissolved, its remnants either filtering back into the villages or being absorbed into the Song regional garrisons. Judged as a single rising, it changed neither the strategic balance between Song and Jin nor the outcome of any decisive pitched battle. But the stockades it held and the years it bought were, during the weakest two decades of the new Southern Song, the only resistance still operating in the north, and they left later readers with the knowledge that resistance to the Jin never truly stopped outside the regular army of the court.
